forwardMerge.how: I computed both myself, with the procedure of skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md, after a `jj git fetch`: the fingerprint at the head my last E2E line names (130911b16c93) is 5846cf7e…, and at the merge head ba3dad8b…. The first equals the implementer's own before-value at a648cb09, which is right, since a648cb09 differs from 130911b16c93 only under .legion, the fileset the check leaves out. So my old head and its own old head are the same diff, and the merge changed it. A changed fingerprint is a full round, which is what this is, and the implementer's forward-merge comment says `changed` too and names the files.
forwardMerge.whatMainMoved: This merge is not cosmetic, which is why the full round matters: main moved internal/broker/ratelimit to internal/ratelimit, made config.APIAccounts a map[string]api.Account (so SignIn moved from config to approval to break an import cycle), gave accountAuth a second argument, took migration number 0021 (the branch's two became 0022_browser_sessions and 0023_signin_status), and rewrote scripts/dev-broker.sh. Every one of those is under the branch's own code, so I re-drove the live binary rather than trusting the suites.

workspace: The pod was replaced again overnight (podUid 6d8f65fd, generation 7) after the 03:02Z release roll, and my workspace was recreated. I checked it against what I did: it stands on the pushed branch, clean, and my round-7 handoff 405f9059c298 is in the ancestry. The disk is fresh, so this pod carried no Postgres and no browser of mine: I used the Postgres LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN names (PostgreSQL 18.6, login legion_test) and had to install Chromium myself — the browser suite first failed 54 of 54 in about 400 ms each with `browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at /legion/scratch/cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1248/…`, and `bunx playwright install chromium` fixed it. That first run is an installation failure, not a result; the run I report is the one after it. A role that comes to a fresh pod needs that install before the browser suite says anything.

observationsForTheReviewer: A fresh pod has no browser for Dispatch's suite. Mine failed 54 of 54 in about 400 ms each until `bunx playwright install chromium` downloaded chromium_headless_shell-1248 to /legion/scratch/cache/ms-playwright. Worth knowing before a count like that is read as a result.

cmd/agent-secrets does not finish inside go's default ten-minute timeout in this pod: my first run reported the right 13 failures and then `panic: test timed out after 10m0s` at 600.1 s, leaving the rest of the package unrun. With `-timeout 30m` it completes in 614 s with those same 13 and nothing else. CI gives that lane 20 minutes, so CI is unaffected; a role running it by hand should pass the flag.

internal/broker/store now fails two IAM tests in a Legion pod rather than one, because the pod's shared Postgres authenticates by trust and its login may not create or drop roles. Both are in iam_test.go, which the branch does not touch.

Standing from earlier rounds, neither a failure: a signed-in person of the domain who is not the approver is served the whole record page with no decision form, which the spec's design describes; and the page's routes share one per-address bucket with Dispatch's ServiceAccount traffic, so a deployment with a load balancer and BROKER_TRUSTED_PROXY_HEADER unset would key every browser on one address.
